dependencies.why: needs terrain, and a real mesh with a real material -- without one it places /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube. Author the texture and master material FIRST, then the mesh, then scatter. Placing geometry before its surface exists is how blockout gets mistaken for finished work.

capture verifies an existing system; author or inspect first

poll after a prior partially_completed response
a master samples the textures it wires; generate them first
a mesh without a surface is a grey solid; author the material before the geometry that wears it

import is a source of geometry, not a consumer -- it runs before anything that places a mesh, and is the alternative to SubmitMeshOps when the result must match a reference rather than merely read as a tree
layers may sample textures; author or import them first
there must be a landscape to snap onto
